questions.question: Jane takes four weeks of annual leave. Her weekly pay is \$550 and her annual leave loading is $17\frac12\%$ of four weeks pay. What is Jane's total pay for this period of annual leave, rounded to the nearest dollar?
A football game is being played in New York (UTC−5), starting at 12:30 pm on Friday. What is the time in Sydney (UTC+10) when the game starts in New York?
questions.answer: Sydney is $10 - (-5) = 15$ hours ahead: 12:30 pm Friday + 15 h = 3:30 am Saturday. **(C)**

questions.question: This set of data is arranged in order from smallest to largest: 5, 7, 10, $x$, 12, 19, 25. The range is four less than twice the value of $x$. Which one of the following is true?
options: The median is 12 and the interquartile range is 20.
The median is 12 and the interquartile range is 12.
The median is 11 and the interquartile range is 20.
The median is 11 and the interquartile range is 12.

questions.question: A bag contains 150 jelly beans. Some of them are blue and the rest are green. The ratio of blue to green jelly beans is $1 : 4$. Timothy eats 5 of each colour. What is the new ratio of blue to green jelly beans in simplest form?
A network with source A and sink B is shown. The capacities of the two paths are labelled. The cut shown on the diagram has a capacity of 30. Which of the following statements is correct?
questions.answer: Every cut's capacity is an upper bound on the flow, so the maximum flow is at most 30. It equals 30 only if this is the minimum cut, which isn't known. **(C)**
options: The maximum flow is 30 or less.
The maximum flow is 30 or more.

questions.question: Joseph is a personal trainer. He records his client's weight as part of his training regime. How can this data be classified?
questions.answer: Weight is measured, not counted: continuous numerical. **(A)**

A spinner with 6 sections has an equal number of red and green sections. This spinner is spun twice. What is the probability of the same colour, when the spinner is spun twice?
The diagram shows a triangle $ABC$ where $AC = 55$ cm, $AB = 30$ cm, $\angle BCA = 28^\circ$ and angle $ABC$ is obtuse. What is the size of the obtuse angle $ABC$, to the nearest degree?
questions.answer:
$$\frac{\sin B}{55} = \frac{\sin 28^\circ}{30} \Rightarrow \sin B \approx 0.8607 \Rightarrow B \approx 59.4^\circ$$
$B$ is obtuse, so $B = 180^\circ - 59.4^\circ \approx 121^\circ$. **(B)**

questions.question: An item was purchased for \$770, including 10% GST. What is the amount of GST included in the price?
An object is projected vertically into the air. Its height, $h$ metres, above the ground after $t$ seconds is given by $h(t) = -5t^2 + 80t$. For how long is the object 200 m or higher in the air?
questions.answer:
$-5t^2 + 80t = 200 \Rightarrow t^2 - 16t + 40 = 0 \Rightarrow t = 8 \pm \sqrt{24} \approx 3.1$ or $12.9$.

It is at or above 200 m for about $12.9 - 3.1 \approx 9.8$ s, closest to 10 seconds. **(A)**

questions.question: The distribution for delivery times for pizza from House of Pizzas follows a normal distribution, with a mean of 25 minutes and standard deviation 5 minutes. What percentage of pizzas have a delivery of greater than 30 minutes?
questions.answer: 30 minutes is $z = 1$. About 68% lie within one standard deviation, so $\frac{32\%}{2} = 16\%$ lie above. **(D)**

questions.question: Which of the following could be the graph $y = -2x - 2$?
questions.answer: Negative gradient and $y$-intercept $-2$ (so it crosses the $x$-axis at $x = -1$). **(B)**

questions.question: Joan takes out a loan of \$7000 for 6 years. Simple interest is charged on the loan. The loan will charge a total of \$3360 of interest over the 6 years. What is the simple interest rate per annum charged on the loan?
A network contains 16 vertices. How many edges are required to form a spanning tree?
questions.answer: A spanning tree on $n$ vertices has $n - 1 = 15$ edges. **(C)**

questions.question:
The graph of the quadratic function represented by the equation $y = x^2 - 11x + 18$ is shown. It passes through $(0, 18)$, $(2, 0)$ and $(9, 0)$.

Find the values of $x$ and $y$ at the turning point of the graph.

The graph of the quadratic function represented by the equation $y = x^2 - 11x + 18$ is shown. It passes through $(0, 18)$, $(2, 0)$ and $(9, 0)$.

The graph shows $y = 18$ when $x = 0$. What is the other value of $x$ for which $y = 18$?
questions.answer: By symmetry about $x = 5.5$: $x = 2 \times 5.5 - 0 = 11$.

questions.question:
A thin pole stands vertically in the middle of a level playing ground. From point $A$ on the ground, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole, $T$, is 18°. From point $B$, also on the ground but 5.35 metres further from the foot of the pole than $A$, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 15°.

Draw a sketch to represent this information.
questions.answer: A right triangle with the pole (height $y$) on one side; $A$ and $B$ on the ground, $B$ 5.35 m further out. The angles of elevation are $18^\circ$ at $A$ and $15^\circ$ at $B$, so $\angle BAT = 162^\circ$ and $\angle ATB = 3^\circ$.

questions.question:
A thin pole stands vertically in the middle of a level playing ground. From point $A$ on the ground, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole, $T$, is 18°. From point $B$, also on the ground but 5.35 metres further from the foot of the pole than $A$, the angle of elevation to the top of the pole is 15°.

Determine the height of the pole.
questions.answer:
In $\triangle ABT$: $\angle BAT = 180^\circ - 18^\circ = 162^\circ$ and $\angle ATB = 18^\circ - 15^\circ = 3^\circ$.
$$\frac{BT}{\sin 162^\circ} = \frac{5.35}{\sin 3^\circ} \Rightarrow BT \approx 31.58\text{ m}$$
$$y = 31.58 \sin 15^\circ \approx 8.18\text{ m}$$

questions.question:
A plumber leases equipment which is valued at \$55 000. The salvage value of the equipment at any time can be calculated using either of the two methods of depreciation shown in the table.

| Method of depreciation | Rate of depreciation |
|---|---|
| Straight line depreciation | \$4000 per annum |
| Declining-balance depreciation | 10% p.a. |

Under which method of depreciation would the salvage value of the equipment be lower at the end of 5 years? Justify your answer with appropriate mathematical calculations.
questions.answer:
- Straight line: $S = 55\,000 - 4000 \times 5 = \$35\,000$
- Declining balance: $S = 55\,000(0.9)^5 \approx \$32\,476.95$

The **declining-balance** method gives the lower salvage value.

Calculate the Pearson's correlation coefficient for the data, correct to two decimal places.

Identify the direction and the strength of the linear association between blood cholesterol level and hours exercised.

The graphs of the probability density functions of three normally distributed random variables $W$, $X$ and $Y$ are shown below.

State, with justification, which of the three random variables has the largest mean.
questions.answer: **$Y$**: its curve is centred furthest to the right (the peak of a normal curve is at the mean).

questions.question:
The graphs of the probability density functions of three normally distributed random variables $W$, $X$ and $Y$ are shown below.

State, with justification, which of the three random variables has the smallest standard deviation.
questions.answer: **$X$**: its curve is the tallest and narrowest, so its data is least spread out.

questions.question: Is this graph Eulerian? Justify your answer with mathematical reasoning.
questions.answer:
Degrees: top-left vertex 1, middle-left vertex 4, top-middle vertex 3 (straight edge, arc and edge to the right), right vertex 2, bottom-middle vertex 2, bottom-left vertex 2.

Exactly two vertices (top-left and top-middle) have odd degree. So the graph has an **Euler trail** (starting at one odd vertex and finishing at the other) and is semi-Eulerian, but it is **not Eulerian**: an Euler circuit needs every vertex to have even degree.

*Note: the school's solution says "2 odd vertices, therefore Eulerian", which describes an Euler trail rather than an Euler circuit.*

questions.question:
The weights of students in a class were recorded. The results for this class are displayed in the cumulative frequency graph shown (25 students).

The lightest student in the class weighed 40 kg and the heaviest in the class weighed 90 kg.

Construct a box-plot for this class, using a number line.
questions.answer:
With 25 students, read across from cumulative frequencies of about 6.25 ($Q_1$), 12.5 (median) and 18.75 ($Q_3$) to the ogive, then down to the weight axis.

Five-number summary (approximately): min 40, $Q_1 \approx 51$, median $\approx 60$, $Q_3 \approx 67$, max 90. Draw whiskers from 40 to $Q_1$ and from $Q_3$ to 90, with a box from $Q_1$ to $Q_3$ split at the median.

(The school's solution reads $Q_1 = 54$, median $= 61$ and $Q_3 = 66$; values read from a graph will vary slightly.)

questions.question:
A bag contains 4 red balls and 5 black balls. Two balls are selected at random without replacement. A partially completed tree diagram is shown below.

Complete the probability tree diagram and calculate the probability of selecting two balls of the same colour.
questions.answer:
- First selection: $P(R) = \frac49$, $P(B) = \frac59$
- After $R$: $P(R) = \frac38$, $P(B) = \frac58$
- After $B$: $P(R) = \frac48$, $P(B) = \frac48$

$$P(\text{same}) = \frac49 \times \frac38 + \frac59 \times \frac48 = \frac{12}{72} + \frac{20}{72} = \frac49$$

questions.question:
Sonya and James each invest \$2000 for 10 years.
- Sonya's investment earns simple interest at a rate of 5.5% per annum.
- James' investment earns an interest rate of 4.5% per annum, compounding quarterly.

By calculating the interest earned over the 10 years, determine who will have the greater amount.
questions.answer:
- Sonya: $I = 2000 \times 0.055 \times 10 = \$1100$
- James: $FV = 2000\left(1 + \frac{0.045}{4}\right)^{40} \approx \$3128.75$, so $I = \$1128.75$

**James** will have the greater amount.

questions.question:
A bowl of hot soup is cooling on a table. Its temperature, $T$°C, after $t$ minutes is given by the formula $T = 100(1.075)^{-t}$.

Calculate the temperature of the soup after 2.5 minutes.

A bowl of hot soup is cooling on a table. Its temperature, $T$°C, after $t$ minutes is given by the formula $T = 100(1.075)^{-t}$.

What is the vertical intercept of this function and what does it represent?
questions.answer: At $t = 0$: $T = 100(1.075)^0 = 100$. The intercept is 100°C, the temperature of the soup at the start.

questions.question: Jack and Jill are going to the beach 5 km away. Jill will ride her bike at 12 km/h while Jack will jog at 8 km/h. How much head start should Jill give Jack so that they arrive at the beach at the same time?
questions.answer:
- Jack: $t = \frac58 = 0.625$ h $= 37.5$ min
- Jill: $t = \frac{5}{12} \approx 0.4167$ h $= 25$ min

Head start $= 37.5 - 25 = 12.5$ minutes.

questions.question:

Draw a minimum spanning tree connecting all 7 towns.
questions.answer: Kruskal's algorithm: $AC$ 1, $CE$ 2, $AB$ 3, $DE$ 3, $AG$ 4, $EF$ 4 (6 edges for 7 towns).

questions.question:
The graph represents the length in km between seven towns. The towns must be connected by power lines which cost \$700 000 per kilometre. The towns only need to be linked by one line – the entire network is not being constructed.

What is the minimum cost of connecting the towns? Justify your decision mathematically.
questions.answer:
Length of the minimum spanning tree $= 1 + 2 + 3 + 3 + 4 + 4 = 17$ km.
$$\text{Cost} = 17 \times 700\,000 = \$11\,900\,000$$

questions.question:
The following formula can be used to calculate an estimate for blood alcohol content (BAC) for females.
$$BAC_{\text{female}} = \frac{10N - 7.5H}{5.5M}$$
where $N$ is the number of standard drinks consumed, $H$ is the number of hours drinking and $M$ is the person's weight in kilograms.

Samantha weighs 65 kg. Her BAC was zero when she began drinking alcohol. At 10:00 pm, after consuming 4 standard drinks, her BAC was 0.04.

Using the formula, estimate at what time Samantha began drinking alcohol, to the nearest minute.
questions.answer:
$$0.04 = \frac{10(4) - 7.5H}{5.5(65)} \Rightarrow 14.3 = 40 - 7.5H \Rightarrow H \approx 3.4267\text{ h} \approx 3\text{ h }26\text{ min}$$
10:00 pm − 3 h 26 min $=$ **6:34 pm**.

questions.question: Use forward and backward scanning to identify the critical path. (Activities: $A$ 7, $B$ 1, $C$ 5, $D$ 2, $E$ 4, $F$ 5, $G$ 1, $H$ 1.)
questions.answer:
Forward scan: 0, 7, 8, 10 (after $D$), 12 (after $E$), 15 (after $F$), 16 (finish). The backward scan gives the same latest times along $A$–$B$–$D$–$F$–$H$.

Critical path: **A, B, D, F, H** (16).

questions.question: The marks, $x$, obtained by students in a maths exam were normally distributed with a mean of 85 and a standard deviation of 4. If the top 2.5% of students received an A, what was the minimum score to achieve an A?
questions.answer: The top 2.5% is $z > 2$: $x = 85 + 2 \times 4 = 93$.

questions.question:
A cake is created using a cylinder and a hemisphere shaped top. The cylinder has a height of 10 cm and the hemisphere has a radius of 7 cm.

Calculate the surface area of the cake that is to be covered in icing (not including the base), correct to the nearest cm².
questions.answer:
Curved surface of the cylinder plus the hemisphere:
$$SA = 2\pi rh + 2\pi r^2 = 2\pi(7)(10) + 2\pi(7)^2 \approx 439.82 + 307.88 \approx 748\text{ cm}^2$$

questions.question: An oil tanker hits a reef in the Pacific ocean and releases oil from its reservoirs. The oil slick extends 10 km NE from the tanker and from the air can be seen to turn to a bearing of 158° for 25 km, then back to the tanker. Calculate the area of the oil slick.
questions.answer:
The first leg is on a bearing of $045^\circ$. At the turn, the angle between the back bearing ($225^\circ$) and $158^\circ$ is $225^\circ - 158^\circ = 67^\circ$ (equivalently $180^\circ - 45^\circ - (158^\circ - 90^\circ)$).
$$A = \tfrac12 \times 10 \times 25 \times \sin 67^\circ \approx 115.06\text{ km}^2$$

questions.question: A full container has 5.2 L of a mixture of cordial and water in the ratio $1 : 3$. After removing 1.6 L of the mixture, more water is added to refill the container. What is the ratio of cordial to water in the final mixture?
questions.answer:
Remaining mixture: $5.2 - 1.6 = 3.6$ L, i.e. 0.9 L cordial and 2.7 L water.

Add 1.6 L water: $0.9 : 4.3 = 9 : 43$.

questions.question:
Willow's business Fashion Face Masks makes and sells embroidered face masks. Willow purchases plain cloth masks and embroiders them with different patterns. The cost of each plain mask is \$4 and Willow sells the embroidered masks for \$10 each. Willow invests \$420 in an embroidery machine and a thread kit to make 100 masks.

The production cost and revenue generated from the sale of the embroidered masks can be modelled with two linear equations, as shown in the graph.

Using the graph, solve the two equations simultaneously and explain the significance of this solution for Willow's business.
questions.answer: The lines $R = 10n$ and $C = 4n + 420$ meet at $(70, 700)$: this is the **break-even point**. Selling 70 masks brings in \$700, exactly covering costs.

questions.question: A soccer goal is 8 m wide. A player shoots for goal when he is 20 m from one post and 15 m from the other post. Within what angle must the shot be made to score a goal?
questions.answer: $$\cos\theta = \frac{20^2 + 15^2 - 8^2}{2 \times 20 \times 15} = \frac{561}{600} = 0.935 \Rightarrow \theta \approx 20.77^\circ$$

questions.question:
The table shows the income tax rate for Australian residents for the 2025 – 2026 financial year.

| Taxable income | Tax on this income |
|---|---|
| 0 – \$18 200 | Nil |
| \$18 201 – \$45 000 | 16c for each \$1 over \$18 200 |
| \$45 001 – \$135 000 | \$4288 plus 30c for each \$1 over \$45 000 |
| \$135 001 – \$190 000 | \$31 288 plus 37c for each \$1 over \$135 000 |
| \$190 001 and over | \$51 638 plus 45c for each \$1 over \$190 000 |

At the end of the 2025 – 2026 financial year, Kale's tax payable was \$154 536, excluding the Medicare levy. What was Kale's taxable income?
questions.answer:
That much tax is only possible in the top bracket:
$$154\,536 = 51\,638 + 0.45(x - 190\,000) \Rightarrow x - 190\,000 = \frac{102\,898}{0.45} \approx 228\,662.22$$
$$x \approx \$418\,662.22$$

questions.question: Sam believes he did better on his Math exam than his Physics exam. The Physics exam had a mean score of 55 and a standard deviation of 17 and he achieved 67 out of 100. On the Math exam, he achieved 72 out of 100 and the class had a mean of 64 and a standard deviation of 12. Evaluate the reasonableness of Sam's statement, using mathematical reasoning.
questions.answer:
$$z_{\text{physics}} = \frac{67 - 55}{17} \approx 0.71, \qquad z_{\text{math}} = \frac{72 - 64}{12} \approx 0.67$$
Sam is **not** correct: relative to the class he did slightly better in Physics.

questions.question: A plumber needs to fix a system of pipes from source $S$ to sink $t$ (network shown). The plumber experienced difficulty in cutting the pipes and wants to identify the smallest cut possible (in terms of capacity). By finding the maximum flow, explain why this is the smallest cut possible. Justify your response on the diagram below.
questions.answer:
Pushing flow along augmenting paths saturates the pipes $3$, $2$, $2$ and $5$ shown in the solution, giving a maximum flow of 12. The cut through these saturated pipes has capacity
$$3 + 2 + 2 + 5 = 12.$$
By the maximum-flow minimum-cut theorem, no cut can be smaller than the maximum flow, so this is the minimum cut. (It passes only through saturated pipes, or pipes flowing back towards the source.)
